_note: New Hampshire landlord-entry rules, retrieved verbatim from the NH General Court statute site (gc.nh.gov; the legacy gencourt.state.nh.us host now 301-redirects here) on 2026-06-20. RSA 540-A:3, IV: no landlord shall willfully enter the tenant's premises without prior consent, other than to make emergency repairs. RSA 540-A:3, V-d: a landlord may enter without consent ONLY to make emergency repairs (paragraphs IV and IV-a) or under a court order obtained pursuant to RSA 540-A:4. Enforcement: a violation of RSA 540-A:3 is actionable under RSA 540-A:4 and carries the consumer-protection remedies of RSA 358-A:10. status=draft-unverified: must be reviewed by a NH tenant attorney / legal-aid clinic before public conclusions.

rules.title: Landlord may enter without notice or consent (non-emergency)
rules.description: Per RSA 540-A:3, IV, a landlord may not willfully enter the tenant's premises without prior consent, except to make emergency repairs. A clause giving the landlord a right to enter at will, at any time, or without notice or consent for ordinary (non-emergency) purposes — inspections, showings, maintenance — contradicts the statute.
rules.tenant_explainer: Outside a real emergency, your landlord can't just let themselves in — New Hampshire requires your prior consent. A lease line saying they may enter 'at any time' or 'without notice' for inspections or showings doesn't hold up.

citations.label: N.H. RSA 540-A:3, IV
citations.quote: No landlord shall willfully enter into the premises of the tenant without prior consent, other than to make emergency repairs.

citations.label: N.H. RSA 540-A:3, V-d
citations.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, a landlord may only enter a tenant's dwelling unit without the consent of the tenant: (a) To make emergency repairs pursuant to paragraphs IV and IV-a; or (b) If the landlord has obtained an order authorizing the entry from a court of competent jurisdiction pursuant to RSA 540-A:4.
